reference_title: Design, Analysis, and Testing of Laterally Loaded Deep Foundations that Support Transportation Facilities

sections.title: Overview
sections.summary: Covers non-gravity cantilevered walls with discrete vertical elements (drilled shafts, driven or drilled-in piles) embedded for passive resistance: top-down, soldier pile or beam and lagging walls, elements generally at least three effective diameters apart with lagging or panels between (Figure 9-1). Closer spacing overlaps passive influence; continuous walls see Brown et al. (2010).
sections.body: The chapter is limited to non-gravity cantilevered walls with discrete vertical wall elements, such as drilled shafts, driven piles or drilled-in piles, embedded below finish grade to provide passive resistance to the retained earth. Often called top-down walls, soldier pile walls or beam and lagging walls, their supporting shafts or piles are spaced center-to-center generally at least three effective diameters apart, with fascia lagging, precast concrete panels, or temporary lagging with a cast-in-place concrete facing, between the above grade portions of the vertical elements (Figure 9-1). Center-to-center spacing less than three diameters may overlap the passive stress influence of the supporting elements. Analysis of continuous vertical wall elements (secant or tangent pile walls) is discussed in Brown et al. (2010). (p. 127)
key_points: Non-gravity cantilevered walls with discrete vertical elements (p. 127).
Elements generally at least three effective diameters apart center-to-center (p. 127).
Closer spacing may overlap passive stress influence (p. 127).
Secant and tangent pile walls: see Brown et al. (2010) (p. 127).
sections.applicability: Non-gravity cantilevered retaining walls with discrete vertical deep foundation elements at spacing of at least 3 diameters

sections.title: Earth Pressures
sections.summary: Before p-y analysis, resolve active pressure above the lagging base, with surcharges, into a resultant: Pa = Ka gamma' l H^2/2 at H/3 (Eq. 9-1, AASHTO 3.11), Ka by Coulomb with wall friction (Eqs. 9-2, 9-3; Figure 9-2; delta from Table 9-1). Temporary walls in clay: at least 0.25 times effective overburden or 0.035 ksf/ft. Add water pressure if not drained.
sections.body: Before p-y analysis of the discrete supporting elements, the active earth pressures above the base of the lagging or panels must be resolved into a resultant force, including surcharge loads above the wall (the print reads "Prior to a performing"). AASHTO Section 3.11 gives the unfactored resultant active earth pressure for permanent non-gravity cantilevered walls, Eq. 9-1, acting at H/3 above the design base grade, the bottom of the panel or lagging below finish grade in front of the wall. Ka is from Coulomb theory with wall friction, Eq. 9-2 (p. 128) with Eq. 9-3; the geometric variables are illustrated in Figure 9-2. Suggested interface friction angles from AASHTO Table 3.11.5.3-1 (U.S. Department of the Navy, Design Manual 7.02, 1986) are in Table 9-1 (p. 129): mass concrete on clean sound rock 35 degrees (tan delta 0.70), on clean gravel and coarse sand 29 to 31 (0.55 to 0.60), on clean fine to medium sand or silty or clayey gravel 24 to 29 (0.45 to 0.55), on clean fine sand or silty or clayey fine to medium sand 19 to 24 (0.34 to 0.45), on fine sandy or nonplastic silt 17 to 19 (0.31 to 0.34), on very stiff and hard residual or preconsolidated clay 22 to 26 (0.40 to 0.49), on medium stiff and stiff clay and silty clay 17 to 19 (0.31 to 0.34); steel piles on clean gravel or well-graded rock fill 22 (0.40), on clean sand or single size hard rock fill 17 (0.31), on silty sand or gravel or sand mixed with silt or clay 14 (0.25), on fine sandy or nonplastic silt 11 (0.19); formed or precast concrete on clean gravel or well-graded rock fill 22 to 26 (0.40 to 0.49), on clean sand or single-size hard rock fill 17 to 22 (0.31 to 0.40), on silty sand or gravel or sand with silt or clay 17 (0.31), on fine sandy or nonplastic silt 14 (printed ".25"). Some ground movement beyond that needed for active pressure may be required for full wall friction, influenced by how the lagging or panels are installed. Long-term pressures from stiff clays and plastic silts on permanent structures are generally controlled by effective stress strength. For temporary walls in cohesive soils, active pressure may use total stress methods and undrained strength, but not less than 0.25 times the effective overburden pressure at any depth or 0.035 ksf/ft of wall height, whichever is greater (AASHTO 2014); for soft to medium-stiff clays, lateral loads are typically governed by undrained (total stress) strength (AASHTO Section 3.11); effective and total stress strength of cohesive soils is in GEC-5 (Loehr et al. 2016). If hydrostatic pressure cannot be relieved by drainage behind the lagging or fascia, water pressure is added to earth pressure computed with submerged unit weights. (pp. 127 to 129)
key_points: Resolve active pressure above the lagging base, with surcharges, into a resultant (p. 127).
Pa = Ka gamma' l H^2 / 2 at H/3 above design base grade (Eq. 9-1, AASHTO 3.11) (p. 127).
Coulomb Ka with wall friction (Eqs. 9-2, 9-3; Figure 9-2) (pp. 127 to 128).
Interface friction angles from DM 7.02 in Table 9-1 (p. 129).
Temporary walls in clay: at least 0.25 times effective overburden or 0.035 ksf/ft, whichever greater (p. 129).
Add water pressure if it cannot be drained (p. 129).
equations: Eq. 9-1: Pa = Ka gamma' l H^2 / 2; unfactored resultant active earth pressure for permanent non-gravity cantilevered walls (AASHTO Section 3.11), acting at H/3 above the design base grade, H = total wall height measured from the panel or lagging base level, gamma' = effective unit weight of the retained soil, l = contributory length of wall relative to each vertical element (center-to-center spacing) (p. 127)
Eq. 9-2: ka = sin^2(theta + phi'f) / (r [sin^2(theta) sin(theta - delta)]); Coulomb active earth pressure coefficient including wall friction (p. 127)

Eq. 9-3: r = [1 + sqrt( sin(phi'f + delta) sin(phi'f + beta) / (sin(theta - delta) sin(theta + beta)) )]^2; delta = friction angle between backfill and wall, beta = angle of backfill with respect to horizontal, theta = angle of back face of wall to horizontal (normally 90 degrees), phi'f = effective angle of internal friction of the retained soil; geometry in Figure 9-2 (p. 128)
figures: Figure 9-2: Geometry for active earth pressure

sections.title: Determination of Embedment Depth
sections.summary: Embedment is assessed by p-y software (or limit equilibrium) with the factored resultant applied directly or as shear and moment at design grade, taken at the bottom of the fascia panel or lower for disturbance such as utility trenching; Strength Limit loads (AASHTO 3.4.1) and resistance factor 0.75 for passive resistance (AASHTO 11.5.6-1).
sections.body: With the resultant active earth pressure above design grade (base of lagging or panel fascia) determined, p-y software can assess the embedment of the vertical elements, by applying the factored resultant directly to the pile/shaft or, depending on the program, resolving it into an applied shear and moment at design grade. Design grade for passive resistance should be taken at the bottom of the fascia panel (below finish grade in front of the wall) to model construction, and a lower level considered for disturbance during the wall's service life, such as utility trenching. Limit equilibrium methods can also be used. Following Chapter 5 (Section 5.1, Block 9.1), the required embedment follows from a geotechnical strength limit analysis of individual elements with the factored strength limit load combinations of AASHTO Section 3.4.1 and a geotechnical resistance factor of 0.75 for passive resistance of the embedded piles or shafts, as per AASHTO 11.5.6-1. (p. 130)
key_points: Embedment by p-y software with the factored resultant or equivalent shear and moment (p. 130).
Design grade at the bottom of the fascia panel; lower for future disturbance (p. 130).
Limit equilibrium methods may also be used (p. 130).
sections.applicability: Determination of required pile/shaft embedment depth for soldier pile and lagging retaining walls at Strength Limit State

sections.title: Evaluation of Deformation
sections.summary: After embedment and Structural Strength (Chapter 11) are satisfied, service load combinations (AASHTO 3.4.1) in a p-y analysis assess deflection (Chapter 5, Block 9.3); if shear and moment were applied at design grade, project the translation and rotation there to the top of the wall.
sections.body: After the pile or shaft embedment and the Structural Strength Limit State (Chapter 11) are satisfied, the service load combinations of AASHTO 3.4.1 are used in a p-y analysis to assess deflection, as discussed in Chapter 5 (Section 5.1, Block 9.3). If the p-y analysis uses resolved shear and moment at the design grade elevation, the free-head lateral translation and angular distortion computed at design grade must be projected to the top of the wall. (p. 130)
key_points: Service load combinations (AASHTO 3.4.1) in p-y analysis for deflection (p. 130).
Check after embedment and Structural Strength are satisfied (p. 130).
Project design grade translation and rotation to the top of the wall (p. 130).
sections.applicability: Lateral deflection evaluation of soldier pile and lagging walls at Service Limit State
